x-http.notes: Unchanged from specs/done/005-mcp-morning-green-receipt/contracts/list_invoices.json: POST /documents/search with filters in JSON body. Feature 038 adds internal pagination (looping this same endpoint across pages) and reads total/page/pages fields from the response (research.md Decision 1) - no change to the request contract below.

x-response-behavior.notes: Feature 038 addendum (input schema above is unchanged; this documents the tool's OUTPUT contract, which is not itself expressed as JSON Schema since the tool returns a formatted Hebrew string, not structured data). Updated 2026-08-04 to add the token-budget truncation dimension (research.md Decision 5); a same-day revision mistakenly lowered the value to a permanent 800 (Decision 6), corrected by a third round of review (Decision 7) back to the real 2500 default, now sourced from config (MorningMCPConfig.list_invoices_token_budget) rather than a hardcoded constant.
x-response-behavior.token_budget_source: MorningMCPConfig.list_invoices_token_budget (config.json field, default 2500) - NOT a hardcoded constant; raising/lowering the real production value is a config change only.
x-response-behavior.within_cap_fits_budget: Loops every Morning page needed to fetch the complete raw result set matching status/from_date/to_date/client_name, applies local status filtering, and - if the fully formatted reply is within the token budget - returns a Hebrew string starting with a precomputed exact count line, followed by one block per matching invoice.
x-response-behavior.within_cap_exceeds_budget: Same fetch as above, but the formatted reply would exceed the token budget: returns only the largest prefix of invoice blocks that fits, with a 'showing X of Y' count line and a closing note that more results were omitted because the reply would otherwise be too long, asking the user to narrow the search. Confirmed live to be common for real data (~280 tokens/invoice block), not a rare edge case.
x-response-behavior.over_cap: Fetches only the first Morning page (to read the real total), fetches no further pages, and returns a Hebrew refusal message stating the real total and asking the user to narrow the search. No itemized invoice content in this message. Mutually exclusive with the token-budget truncation case above (this path never reaches formatting).
x-response-behavior.zero_matches: Unchanged: returns the existing friendly Hebrew 'no results' message.
